target.title: fix(matrix): fallback to copy+unlink on EXDEV in legacy credentials migration
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

During startup, the Matrix channel loader checks for legacy credentials and attempts to migrate them to the new paths using `fs.renameSync(legacyPath, currentPath)`.

If the legacy path and the current path lie on different mount points or filesystems (for example, when running inside containers or with different volumes), `fs.renameSync` throws an `EXDEV` error ("Cross-device link").

Since this error was caught in an empty `catch {}` block, the file was never migrated, and every future load attempt repeated the failing rename, causing repeated synchronous disk I/O failure overhead.

## Why This Change Was Made

Added a fallback to `fs.copyFileSync` and `fs.unlinkSync` when `fs.renameSync` fails with `EXDEV` code. Proper typescript-compliant error type narrowing is implemented to handle `unknown` catch variables without using `any`.

## User Impact

Matrix configurations across different mounts/filesystems migrate correctly during startup without raising Cross-device link errors, eliminating recurrent disk overhead.

## Evidence

Added unit test `migrates legacy credentials using copy + unlink when renameSync throws EXDEV` in `extensions/matrix/src/matrix/credentials.test.ts` mocking `fs.renameSync` to throw `EXDEV`. Ran tests, and all 13 tests passed.
```bash
 ✓ |extension-matrix| ../../extensions/matrix/src/matrix/credentials.test.ts (13 tests)
   ✓ matrix credentials storage (13)
     ✓ migrates legacy credentials using copy + unlink when renameSync throws EXDEV
```

### Real Behavior Proof

Simulating separate mounts migration startup logs:
```
[matrix-auth] Migrating legacy Matrix credentials from /home/dietpi/.openclaw/credentials/matrix/legacy-ops.json -> /home/dietpi/.openclaw/credentials/matrix/ops.json
[matrix-auth] renameSync failed with EXDEV. Falling back to copyFileSync and unlinkSync.
[matrix-auth] Legacy credential file successfully copied and deleted from legacy path. Matrix authentication active.
```
